newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks seen sideways ahead of budget.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks seen sideways ahead of budget.

text.p: The Singapore stock market is expected to drift mostly sideways on Friday ahead of the budget announcement later in the day.
Finance Minister Richard Hu is expected to start talking about the budget shortly after 0830 GMT, but normally holds off on potentially market-moving comments until after the market is closed.
"The market picked up a bit in late trading yesterday. There could be a bit more short covering ahead of the budget today," said a dealer with a Singapore firm.
Dealers said sentiment would remain cautious on concerns over the weak Malaysian stock market and also speculation over regional currencies.
The Straits Times Industrial index ended down 14.63 points at 1,968.34 on Thursday.
